errors.text: The dominant cause of small-particle loss is assigned to Ostwald ripening and dissolution into larger particles, whereas the target attributes substantial size loss to Au/Cu surface segregation followed by melting and evaporation.
The predicted morphology trend is reversed: the hypothesis proposes spherical-to-faceted evolution, while the observed evolution is elliptical-to-spherical.

The claim that reduced configurational entropy in the core drives phase separation is not adequately justified; the relevant driving force is primarily elemental surface-energy differences coupled to active diffusion.
